english.title: Produce nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation - class C drug
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) produced

(A)_[**(..SPECIFY QUANTITY..)]_
(B)_[a quantity]_

of nitrous oxide, a controlled drug of Class C, in contravention of section 4(1) of the Misuse of Drugs Act 1971, intending to wrongfully inhale it, or knowing or being reckless as to whether it was likely to be wrongfully inhaled by another person
english.legislation: Contrary to section 4(2)(a) of and Schedule 4 to the Misuse of Drugs Act 1971.

english.notes:
(i) This offence is intended to capture those who produce nitrous oxide for themselves or someone else to inhale it for its psychoactive effect. See regulation 4C(2) of the Misuse of Drugs Regulations 2001 which creates a specific exemption from the prohibition on production of nitrous oxide.
(ii) 'Wrongful inhalation' means any inhalation by a person which is not for a medical or dental purpose (for example, the recreational inhalation of nitrous oxide for its psychoactive effect) or is not of nitrous oxide which has been released into the atmosphere (for example, directly from a canister or a balloon), regulation 4C(5). Medical purposes are defined as the purposes of preventative medicine, medical diagnosis or the provision of medical care and treatment, see regulation 2(1) of those regulations.

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 3 months imprisonment and / or fine not exceeding £2,500.
Indictment: maximum 14 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
